75	> Redécoupage faisabilité : **S-05a** = lecteur incrémental sans TUI (critères 3 et 4, effort M) ; **S-05b** = polling dans la vue (critères 1, 2 et 5, effort M).
76	
77	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que la vue se mette à jour pendant qu'une session tourne, afin de suivre la consommation sans relancer de commande.
78	
79	**Critères d'acceptation**
80	1. Étant donné une session active, quand un agent produit un nouveau message, alors ses tokens à l'écran sont à jour en moins de 3 secondes.
81	2. Étant donné un nouveau sous-agent lancé, quand il apparaît, alors il s'ajoute à l'arbre sans quitter la vue.
82	3. Étant donné une session terminée, quand je la regarde, alors plus aucune lecture périodique n'est faite sur ses fichiers.
83	4. La lecture est incrémentale : un transcript de plusieurs Mo n'est pas relu en entier à chaque mise à jour.
84	5. `ctrl+r` force une relecture complète.
85	
86	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: le polling (tick 2 s + stat) ne dégrade pas la réactivité de la TUI (à valider en faisabilité).
87	
88	### S-06 — See each agent's activity and state
89	Epic : E2 — Priorité : Should — Effort : M — Plane : DEVDESK-46
90	
91	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux voir l'état, le nombre d'appels d'outils et la durée de chaque agent, afin de repérer un agent bloqué ou emballé.
92	
93	**Critères d'acceptation**
94	1. Étant donné un agent, quand il est affiché, alors on voit son état (en cours / terminé), son nombre d'appels d'outils et sa durée.
95	2. Étant donné un agent sans nouvelle activité depuis plus de 5 minutes alors qu'il est « en cours », quand la vue se met à jour, alors il est signalé comme inactif.
96	3. Seuls des compteurs sont affichés, jamais le contenu des prompts ni des sorties d'outils.
97	4. Étant donné un sous-agent dont le transcript contient 5 blocs `tool_use` distincts, quand il est affiché, alors son nombre d'appels d'outils est 5, compté depuis le transcript et non depuis la notification de fin (`queued_command.usage.toolUses`, non exploitable : S-01).
98	
99	### S-07 — Indicative cost per agent
100	Epic : E2 — Priorité : Could — Effort : M — Plane : DEVDESK-47
101	
102	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux un coût estimé par agent, afin de situer l'ordre de grandeur.
103	
104	**Critères d'acceptation**
105	1. Étant donné un agent et son modèle, quand le coût est affiché, alors il est marqué comme estimation (tokens × tarif du modèle).
106	2. Étant donné un modèle au tarif inconnu, quand il est affiché, alors la cellule indique `-` et non zéro.
107	3. La table de tarifs est modifiable sans recompiler (configuration).
108	4. Le coût par agent est annoncé comme sous-estimé pour les sous-agents (leur sortie est une borne basse, S-02 critère 6, et une partie des appels API n'est pas dans les transcripts : `cache_read` 24 à 32 % plus haut dans `cost-state`). La cellule garde le marqueur d'estimation du critère 1.
109	5. Étant donné une session terminée dont `cost-state` est disponible, quand le coût est affiché, alors le total facturé de la session est montré avec une ligne « Unattributed » égale au total facturé moins la somme des coûts par agent (ex. total 10,00 $, agents 8,20 $ → Unattributed 1,80 $).
110	6. Étant donné une session en cours (pas de `cost-state`), quand le coût est affiché, alors seuls les coûts estimés par agent apparaissent, sans total facturé ni ligne « Unattributed ».
111	
112	**Hors périmètre** : attribution exacte de la facture par agent, quota.
113	
114	## Epic E3 — Reach sandbox sessions
115	
116	### S-08 — See `sbx` sandbox sessions
117	Epic : E3 — Priorité : Should — Effort : S (option A) ou L (option C/B) — dépend de S-01 — Plane : DEVDESK-48
118	
119	En tant qu'utilisateur travaillant en sandbox, je veux voir aussi les sessions lancées dans `sbx`, afin que la vue couvre mes longues orchestrations.
120	
121	**Critères d'acceptation** : à écrire après S-01 (la solution de transport n'est pas choisie).
122	**Questions ouvertes** : montage de `~/.claude`, hook, ou export OpenTelemetry ?
123	
124	## Won't (cette fois)
125	- Quota 5 h/hebdo (nécessite une statusline concurrente ; `/usage` le couvre).
126	- Historique persisté et comparaison par feature (pas de lien session ↔ story).
127	- Autres CLI d'agents, sessions cloud, OpenTelemetry.
128	
129	## Backlog Plane (créé le 2026-10-24)
130	
131	Projet DEVDESK, état Backlog, label `story`. Les relations « blocked by » n'ont pas pu être créées (l'API de relations répond 404 sur cette édition) : l'ordre de livraison est écrit dans chaque description.

143	| S-07 | DEVDESK-47 | E2 | low | M |
144	| S-08 | DEVDESK-48 | E3 | medium | S à L |

1	# Agent usage monitor : faisabilité (architect, 2026-10-24)
2	
3	**Verdict : faisable, sans nouvelle dépendance Go**, à trois conditions : (1) dédupliquer par `message.id` en gardant la **dernière** ligne, (2) lire les fichiers par polling incrémental dans un `Cmd`, l'agrégat n'étant modifié que dans `Update`, (3) S-08 ne démarre qu'après une vérification sur l'hôte qui lance `sbx`.
4	Légende : [O] observé sur cette machine (structure seulement, aucun contenu lu ni rapporté), [E] estimation.
5	
6	## Observations locales qui changent le plan
7	
8	- [O] 7 projets, 130 JSONL (178 Mo), 91 sous-agents. Plus gros fichier : 15 Mo. **Plus longue ligne : 1,27 Mo** : le `bufio.Scanner` par défaut (64 Kio) échoue. Il faut un `bufio.Reader` ou un `Scanner.Buffer` plafonné, et compter les lignes ignorées.
9	- [O] 19 types de lignes (`assistant`, `user`, `attachment`, `api-request-blob`, `cost-state`, `agent-name`…). Versions 2.1.283 à 2.1.302 seulement : les transcripts plus anciens sont purgés à 30 jours, donc la fixture « autre version » devra être **synthétique**.
10	- [O] **Dédup mesurée** sur tous les transcripts : la somme naïve gonfle les totaux ×1,9 à ×2,5. Garder la *première* ligne sous-estime `output_tokens` de 2,7 %, ce qui dépasse la tolérance de 2 %. La dernière ligne porte toujours le maximum (2968 groupes sur 2968). Il faut aussi exclure le modèle `<synthetic>`.
11	- [O] Le transcript parent ne contient aucune ligne `isSidechain` ni `agentId` : aucun double comptage entre fichiers. Le `toolUseResult` de l'outil Agent n'a pas de `usage`, mais il contient `prompt` : à ne jamais décoder.

2	
3	**Verdict : faisable, sans nouvelle dépendance Go**, à trois conditions : (1) dédupliquer par `message.id` en gardant la **dernière** ligne, (2) lire les fichiers par polling incrémental dans un `Cmd`, l'agrégat n'étant modifié que dans `Update`, (3) S-08 ne démarre qu'après une vérification sur l'hôte qui lance `sbx`.
4	Légende : [O] observé sur cette machine (structure seulement, aucun contenu lu ni rapporté), [E] estimation.
5	
6	## Observations locales qui changent le plan
7	
8	- [O] 7 projets, 130 JSONL (178 Mo), 91 sous-agents. Plus gros fichier : 15 Mo. **Plus longue ligne : 1,27 Mo** : le `bufio.Scanner` par défaut (64 Kio) échoue. Il faut un `bufio.Reader` ou un `Scanner.Buffer` plafonné, et compter les lignes ignorées.
9	- [O] 19 types de lignes (`assistant`, `user`, `attachment`, `api-request-blob`, `cost-state`, `agent-name`…). Versions 2.1.283 à 2.1.302 seulement : les transcripts plus anciens sont purgés à 30 jours, donc la fixture « autre version » devra être **synthétique**.

Garder la *première* ligne sous-estime `output_tokens` de 2,7 %, ce qui dépasse la tolérance de 2 %. La dernière ligne porte toujours le maximum (2968 groupes sur 2968). Il faut aussi exclure le modèle `<synthetic>`.
11	- [O] Le transcript parent ne contient aucune ligne `isSidechain` ni `agentId` : aucun double comptage entre fichiers. Le `toolUseResult` de l'outil Agent n'a pas de `usage`, mais il contient `prompt` : à ne jamais décoder.
12	- [O] `subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json` contient `finished: bool` (87 sur 91 ; absent pour un agent en cours ou une ancienne version) et `spawnDepth` (toujours 1 ici, l'arbre a donc 2 niveaux en pratique). Il contient aussi `description`, un texte de tâche, donc du contenu.
13	- [O] `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` (non documenté) : `sessionId`, `pid`, `status` (`busy` ou `idle`), `updatedAt`. C'est un bon indice pour savoir qu'une session est vivante. Repli : la date de modification du fichier.

Compter les `tool_use` par `(message.id, apiBlockIndex)`, car les lignes streamées répètent le message. Durée = premier → dernier `timestamp`. |
43	| S-07 coût indicatif | **M** | Nouvelle section de configuration (`agent_usage.prices` par modèle, avec les tarifs distincts cache 5 min / 1 h / lecture), `-` si le tarif est inconnu. C'est une carte, pas un scalaire : la vue `:cfg` ne l'édite pas, l'édition passe par le YAML (Q4). |
44	| S-08 sandbox | **S** (option A) à **L** (option B) | Avec l'option A, DevDesk n'ajoute que des racines de transcripts multiples et une colonne « Source » ; le reste est une procédure `sbx` documentée. À réécrire après S-01. |
45	
46	## 3. Packages et intégration
47	
48	- `internal/agentusage` (pur, sans Bubble Tea) : `Discover(roots) []SessionRef`, `type Reader` (offsets et reste, valeur copiable), `ReadDelta(ref, offsets) (Delta, error)`, `type Aggregate` avec `Apply(Delta) Aggregate` (dédup, totaux par agent), `Liveness(ref)` (`sessions/*.json` + mtime). `internal/agentusage/pricing` arrivera avec S-07.
49	- `internal/ui/agentusage` : `Model` (deux niveaux `datatable`, fil d'Ariane sous la table, Règle 123), `availability.go` (Règle 130), `GetHelpContent` (Règle 114), les 4 méthodes de `HeaderView` (compteur de sessions et d'agents dans `GetHeaderInfo`), et l'état de chargement dans le pied de page (Règles 128 et 139).
50	- Points d'entrée : `internal/command/parser.go` (`ViewAgentUsage`, table `viewNames`), `internal/app/command_line.go` (`createView`), `docs/architecture/` (nouveau fichier, et une ligne dans le tableau de `.claude/CLAUDE.md`).
51	- **Commande** : `:usage` / `:us` (Hypothèse : `ag`, `us` et `u` sont libres, à arbitrer en Q1).
52	- **Clavier : aucune lettre d'action en MVP.** `→`/`enter` descend, `←`/`esc` remonte, `.` trie, `/` filtre, `ctrl+r` relit. Les lettres libres (`Q`, `Z`) ne sont pas consommées. Un éventuel filtre « actives seulement » serait une minuscule déclarée dans `keymap.localToggles`. Plus tard : `Y` (copier l'id de session), déjà dans le vocabulaire.
53	- Pas de `jobs.Run` : le polling n'est pas un travail lancé par l'utilisateur. On ne l'inscrit au registre que si l'on veut voir la relecture complète dans `:jobs`, ce qui n'est pas nécessaire.
54	
55	## 4. Sandbox `sbx` : transport
56	
57	D'après des sources tierces, les transcripts d'un `sbx` vivent dans un **volume géré par le kit** et ne sont pas sur l'hôte ; `sbx create` accepte des montages supplémentaires ([sbx/claude-mixin](https://hub.docker.com/r/sbx/claude-mixin), [DEV Community](https://dev.to/thr0n/claude-code-in-docker-sandboxes-239g)). Non vérifié : `sbx` est absent de cette machine.
58	
59	| Option | Avantages | Risques |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| **A. Monter un répertoire hôte dédié** (`~/.devdesk/agent-usage/sbx/<nom>`) comme `~/.claude/projects` du sandbox ; DevDesk le déclare comme racine supplémentaire | Aucun code de transport ; même parseur ; quasi temps réel ; survit à la suppression du sandbox | Il faut recréer le sandbox (`sbx create`) ; le sandbox écrit sur l'hôte. **Ne jamais monter tout `~/.claude`** : le sandbox pourrait écrire `settings.json`/hooks exécutés par l'hôte (évasion). Montages 9p/virtiofs : d'où le polling. |
62	| B. Lire le volume via `sbx exec … tail -c +offset` | Rien à reconfigurer côté sandbox | CLI expérimentale, un processus par tick, latence, dépend de l'auth `sbx` ; effort L |
63	| C. Hook dans le sandbox (`Stop`, `SubagentStop`) qui copie le transcript dans le dépôt monté (`.worktrees/…`) | Utilise le montage existant | Les hooks ne portent pas de tokens (il faut copier le fichier), écrit dans l'arbre du dépôt (gitignore), installe une config dans chaque sandbox, latence par événement |
64	| D. OTel : le sandbox exporte en OTLP vers un récepteur DevDesk | Attribution officielle (`agent_id` sur les événements) | Hors MVP (brief), récepteur à embarquer, sortie réseau du sandbox vers l'hôte via le proxy `sbx`, 5 s/60 s, variables d'environnement par session |
65	
66	**Recommandation : A**, avec un montage **dédié et limité aux transcripts**, sous réserve que S-01 confirme sur l'hôte `sbx` que (a) le montage peut remplacer `~/.claude/projects` sans casser `claude -c`, et (b) les fichiers sont visibles et ajoutés au fil de l'eau côté hôte. Sinon, se replier sur C.
67	
68	## 5. Ordre de livraison
69	
70	1. S-01 (Go / no-go, dédup de référence, constat `sbx`).
71	2. S-02 puis S-05a (même package, en TDD, sans TUI ; parallélisable une fois l'API `Delta`/`Aggregate` figée).
72	3. S-03a, puis S-03b et S-04 (S-04 parallélisable avec S-03b).
73	4. S-05b (critère de succès « en direct < 3 s »).
74	5. S-06, puis S-07 (indépendante, peut glisser), puis S-08 selon S-01.
75	
76	## Questions ouvertes (pour l'utilisateur)
77	
78	1. **Nom de la commande** : `:usage`/`:us` (recommandé), `:agents`/`:ag`, ou `:agent-usage`/`:au` ?
79	2. **Référence des 2 %** : ccusage (externe, règle de dédup à vérifier) ou les lignes `cost-state` de Claude Code (interne, par modèle et non par agent) ? Recommandation : `cost-state` pour le total de session, ccusage en contrôle secondaire.
80	3. **Afficher `meta.description` / `ai-title`** pour distinguer les agents et nommer les sessions ? Ce sont des textes de tâche, contraires à « jamais de contenu ». Recommandation : non en MVP (agent = rôle + `agentId` court, session = projet + date).
81	4. **Tarifs (S-07)** : édition YAML seule acceptable, ou faut-il un éditeur dans `:cfg` (ce qui ajoute M) ?
82	5. **Où tourne `sbx`** : sur l'hôte Windows évoqué dans `.claude/CLAUDE.md` ? DevDesk lit-il alors des chemins Windows (`%USERPROFILE%\.claude`) ? Cela conditionne S-01 et S-08.
83	6. **Recréer les sandboxes** avec un montage supplémentaire (option A) : acceptable ?

1	# Spike S-01 (DEVDESK-39): ccusage gap, sandbox, format drift
2	
3	2026-10-24, this machine (Linux, Node 24.22.1). Structure and numbers only: no transcript content was read into this page.
4	Tool: **ccusage 20.0.43** (npm `latest`, published the same day), via `npx -y ccusage@20.0.43 claude session --id <uuid> --json --breakdown --offline`. The network was available (npx download). Pricing came from the offline cache.
5	
6	## Criterion 1: does ccusage give tokens per sub-agent?
7	
8	Three finished sessions with `subagents/`, all on 2.1.302. "Own" = sum over parent + `subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, keeping the **last** line per `message.id` (map shared by the whole session), with `<synthetic>` excluded. Totals = in + out + cache-read + cache-write.
9	
10	| Session | Sub-agents | Msgs | Per sub-agent? | ccusage total | Own total | Δ own vs ccusage | `cost-state` total | Δ own vs cost-state (total / output) |
11	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
12	| d9acf4b8 (small) | 4 | 77 | **No** | 5,690,886 | 5,690,886 | 0.00 % | 7,060,896 | −19.4 % / −66.7 % |
13	| 8bc69d30 (medium) | 14 | 143 | **No** | 15,659,603 | 15,659,603 | 0.00 % | 20,048,361 | −21.9 % / −58.7 % |
14	| aa37ed75 (large) | 32 | 631 | **No** | 68,172,620 | 68,172,620 | 0.00 % | 84,286,088 | −19.1 % / −66.1 % |
15	
16	- **The gap is confirmed.** ccusage returns one row per session, plus a per-model breakdown with `--breakdown`. Its JSON `entries` carry no agent id. `--by-agent` on the top-level `session` command means *per CLI* (every row is `agent: "claude"`), not per sub-agent. ccusage does read the sub-agent files and counts them in the session total: its entry count equals the number of `message.id`s.
17	- **Dedup.** ccusage matches last-line dedup on every field (0.00 %). Keeping the first line instead loses 0 %, −3.3 % and −23.6 % of `output_tokens`. A naive sum inflates the total ×1.52 / ×1.80 / ×1.95.
18	- **Reference for the 2 % rule: ccusage**, at the session level (it has no per-agent figure to compare against). `cost-state` cannot be the reference:
19	  - it is 19 to 22 % above the transcripts, structurally;
20	  - it is per model, not per agent;
21	  - it is only written when the session closes (34 of 36 files have it only in their last 5 lines; it is missing from the live session).
22	- **Root cause (new, affects S-02/S-07).** On sub-agent messages, the last line per `message.id` has `stop_reason: null` (94 % on 2.1.302, 80 % on 2.1.283), and its `output_tokens` is a streaming placeholder (median 8 tokens).
23	  - The completion notification's `totalTokens` minus the last message's context gives a real output of several hundred tokens for that last message. Sub-agent **output is therefore a lower bound**, in ccusage too.
24	  - `cache_read` is also 24 to 32 % higher in `cost-state`, with no matching `api-request` line (79 requests for 77 messages): those API calls are not in the transcripts.
25	  - Cache-write agrees within 0.7 to 3.2 %. Input tokens differ a lot in relative terms but are negligible in absolute terms. Output weighs ≤ 0.3 % of total tokens, so **ranking agents by tokens is unaffected**; cost per agent is.
26	- A per-agent signal exists in the parent (`attachment.queued_command.usage {totalTokens, toolUses, durationMs}`). But it is linked to its agent only through the notification text (content), and `totalTokens` is the final context size, not a cumulative total. **Not usable.**
27	
28	## Criterion 2: `sbx` transcripts visible from the host: **not verified**
29	
30	`sbx` is not installed on this machine, and the user chose to leave this point open. To run **on the host that runs `sbx`** (not executed here):
31	
32	```bash
33	sbx ls                                                    # pick <name>, a sandbox running claude
34	sbx exec <name> sh -c 'ls -t "$HOME"/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl | head -1; mount | grep -i claude'
35	# on the host, <sid> = the file name printed above, without .jsonl
36	find ~/.claude ~/.devdesk /mnt/c/Users/*/.claude -name '<sid>.jsonl' 2>/dev/null      # WSL/Linux
37	Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter '<sid>.jsonl' "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue  # PowerShell
38	```
39	
40	What to observe and write down:
41	1. Is the file found on the host? Give its path or "not found".
42	2. If found, does its size grow while the agent works (two `stat` calls 10 s apart), and is there a `subagents/` directory next to it?
43	3. From `mount`, is `/home/agent/.claude` a sandbox-private volume? That is what option A (a dedicated transcripts mount) needs to know.
44	
45	## Criterion 3: format drift, 2.1.283 (2026-09-27) to 2.1.302 (2026-10-24)
46	
47	Corpus: 130 parent files and 92 sub-agents; 2.1.283 / .284 / .285 / .302. Version is **per line**: one session spans 2.1.285 → 2.1.302.
48	
49	- **`usage`: additive only.** Nothing removed or renamed. New in 2.1.302: `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`, `service_tier`, `speed`, `inference_geo`, `iterations`, `fallback_credit`. All are **nullable** (null on some lines). `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h` and `server_tool_use.*` are present in both versions.
50	- **Line types.** `api-request` and `api-request-shape` appear in 2.1.302. Sub-agent lines gain `requestedModel`, `requestRef`, `thinkingDurationMs`, `thinkingDisplay` and `attribution*`. 1,086 sub-agent lines carry `agentId` but no `isSidechain`, so filter by **file location**, not by that flag.
51	- **Tree.** `subagents/agent-<17 chars>.jsonl` + `.meta.json` in every version. 2.1.302 adds a sibling `tool-results/` directory (5 of 8 sessions), which discovery must ignore.
52	- **`meta.json`.** `finished` and `launchedWithDefaults` are missing in 2.1.283/285, and in 1 of 92 on 2.1.302: state "unknown". `spawnedWithWorktree`, `worktreeBranch` and `worktreePath` are optional (a path: do not display it).
53	- **The version spread is insufficient**: 19 patch releases of a single minor, all additive. The synthetic "other version" fixture is **still required** for S-02. Include: a renamed or missing `usage` field, an unknown line type, and a `meta.json` without `finished`.
54	
55	## Recommendation: **go with changes**
56	
57	The gap is real: no tool splits by sub-agent. The data is there for input and cache, and ranking holds. The changes:
58	- **S-02**:
59	  - criterion 5 = session total (Σ agents) within 2 % of `ccusage claude session --id`;
60	  - flag sub-agent `output_tokens` as a lower bound when `stop_reason` is null;
61	  - decode the nullable `usage` fields as optional.
62	- **S-03b/S-04**: mark sub-agent "Out" as partial (e.g. `≥`). The sort and the share stay as specified.
63	- **S-07**: per-agent cost under-estimates output. Once `cost-state` exists, show the billed session total and an "Unattributed" remainder.
64	- **S-06**: count `tool_use` blocks from the transcript; do not use the notification.
65	- **S-08 stays blocked** until criterion 2 is run on the `sbx` host.

1	package agentusage
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"strconv"
6	)
7	
8	// lineKind classifies one transcript line.
9	type lineKind int
10	
11	const (
12		kindUsage      lineKind = iota // message.usage present: counts
13		kindNoUsage                    // message with an id, but no usage object
14		kindIgnored                    // valid JSON without a message, or a message with neither id, model nor usage
15		kindUnreadable                 // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
16		kindSynthetic                  // model "<synthetic>": never counts
17	)
18	
19	// record is what decodeLine extracts from a line; only these fields are read.
20	type record struct {
21		MessageID string
22		Model     string
23		Version   string
24		Usage     Tokens
25		StopNull  bool
26	}
27	
28	// syntheticModel is the model name of locally generated, never-billed turns.
29	const syntheticModel = "<synthetic>"
30	
31	// wireLine mirrors the only keys read from a transcript line. Content,
32	// tools and descriptions are deliberately not declared, so encoding/json
33	// skips them without keeping them. The root "type" key is not consulted.
34	type wireLine struct {
35		Version json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
36		Message *wireMessage    `json:"message"`
37	}
38	
39	type wireMessage struct {
40		ID         string          `json:"id"`
41		Model      json.RawMessage `json:"model"`
42		StopReason json.RawMessage `json:"stop_reason"`
43		Usage      *wireUsage      `json:"usage"`
44	}
45	
46	// wireUsage keeps counters raw so a negative, fractional or non-numeric
47	// value can be told apart from an absent one.
48	type wireUsage struct {
49		Input      json.RawMessage `json:"input_tokens"`
50		Output     json.RawMessage `json:"output_tokens"`
51		CacheRead  json.RawMessage `json:"cache_read_input_tokens"`
52		CacheWrite json.RawMessage `json:"cache_creation_input_tokens"`
53	}
54	
55	// decodeLine extracts the usage fields of one transcript line. A message
56	// without usage counts as kindNoUsage only if it has an id or a model (an
57	// assistant turn whose usage went missing or was renamed). It never
58	// reports a decoder error: those can quote line content, so a bad line is
59	// just kindUnreadable.
60	func decodeLine(b []byte) (record, lineKind) {
61		var w wireLine
62		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &w); err != nil {
63			return record{}, kindUnreadable
64		}
65		m := w.Message
66		if m == nil {
67			return record{Version: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version))}, kindIgnored
68		}
69		rec := record{
70			MessageID: m.ID,
71			Model:     sanitizeLabel(optString(m.Model)),
72			Version:   sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version)),
73			StopNull:  isNullOrAbsent(m.StopReason),
74		}
75		switch {
76		case rec.Model == syntheticModel:
77			return rec, kindSynthetic
78		case m.Usage == nil && m.ID == "" && rec.Model == "":
79			// User and tool-result lines carry a message without id, usage or model.
80			return rec, kindIgnored
81		case m.Usage == nil:
82			return rec, kindNoUsage
83		}
84		tokens, ok := m.Usage.tokens()
85		if !ok {
86			return record{}, kindUnreadable
87		}
88		rec.Usage = tokens
89		return rec, kindUsage
90	}
91	
92	// tokens converts the raw counters; ok is false if any is not a
93	// non-negative integer.
94	func (u *wireUsage) tokens() (Tokens, bool) {
95		var t Tokens
96		for _, c := range []struct {
97			raw json.RawMessage
98			dst *int64
99		}{{u.Input, &t.Input}, {u.Output, &t.Output}, {u.CacheRead, &t.CacheRead}, {u.CacheWrite, &t.CacheWrite}} {
100			n, ok := parseCounter(c.raw)
101			if !ok {
102				return Tokens{}, false
103			}
104			*c.dst = n
105		}
106		return t, true
107	}
108	
109	// parseCounter reads one counter; absent or null is 0.
110	func parseCounter(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
111		if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
112			return 0, true
113		}
114		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(string(raw), 10, 64)
115		return n, err == nil && n >= 0
116	}
117	
118	// optString returns the JSON string held by raw, or "" if raw is absent or
119	// of another type: metadata of an unexpected type must not cost the line.
120	func optString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
121		var s string
122		if len(raw) == 0 || raw[0] != '"' || json.Unmarshal(raw, &s) != nil {
123			return ""
124		}
125		return s
126	}
127	
128	// isNullOrAbsent reports whether raw is a missing key or a JSON null. Any
129	// other value, whatever its type, counts as a stop reason being set.
130	func isNullOrAbsent(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
131		return len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null"
132	}

1	package agentusage
2	
3	// Agent is the usage of one agent of a session: the orchestrator (Main) or a
4	// sub-agent.
5	type Agent struct {
6		ID              string
7		Main            bool
8		Type            string // sub-agent type from its meta file; "" if unknown
9		Models          []string
10		Tokens          Tokens
11		Messages        int // distinct message ids
12		PartialMessages int // messages whose last line has no stop reason
13		State           State
14		SpawnDepth      int
15		// key is the table's identity for the agent's lines (the rank of its
16		// transcript); empty means ID. finish clears it from its output.
17		key string
18	}
19	
20	// PartialOutput reports whether some message of the agent was still being
21	// written (no stop reason on its last line), so its output count is a floor.
22	func (a Agent) PartialOutput() bool { return a.PartialMessages > 0 }
23	
24	// IssueKind classifies a line that could not be counted.
25	type IssueKind int
26	
27	const (
28		IssueUnreadable IssueKind = iota // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
29		IssueOversized                   // longer than MaxLineBytes
30		IssueOpenFailed                  // a sub-agent transcript could not be opened

1	package agentusage
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"strconv"
6	)
7	
8	// lineKind classifies one transcript line.
9	type lineKind int
10	
11	const (
12		kindUsage      lineKind = iota // message.usage present: counts
13		kindNoUsage                    // message with an id, but no usage object
14		kindIgnored                    // valid JSON without a message, or a message with neither id, model nor usage
15		kindUnreadable                 // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
16		kindSynthetic                  // model "<synthetic>": never counts
17	)
18	
19	// record is what decodeLine extracts from a line; only these fields are read.
20	type record struct {
21		MessageID string
22		Model     string
23		Version   string
24		Usage     Tokens
25		StopNull  bool
26	}
27	
28	// syntheticModel is the model name of locally generated, never-billed turns.
29	const syntheticModel = "<synthetic>"
30	
31	// wireLine mirrors the only keys read from a transcript line. Content,
32	// tools and descriptions are deliberately not declared, so encoding/json
33	// skips them without keeping them. The root "type" key is not consulted.
34	type wireLine struct {
35		Version json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
36		Message *wireMessage    `json:"message"`
37	}
38	
39	type wireMessage struct {
40		ID         string          `json:"id"`
41		Model      json.RawMessage `json:"model"`
42		StopReason json.RawMessage `json:"stop_reason"`
43		Usage      *wireUsage      `json:"usage"`
44	}
45	
46	// wireUsage keeps counters raw so a negative, fractional or non-numeric
47	// value can be told apart from an absent one.
48	type wireUsage struct {
49		Input      json.RawMessage `json:"input_tokens"`
50		Output     json.RawMessage `json:"output_tokens"`
51		CacheRead  json.RawMessage `json:"cache_read_input_tokens"`
52		CacheWrite json.RawMessage `json:"cache_creation_input_tokens"`
53	}
54	
55	// decodeLine extracts the usage fields of one transcript line. A message
56	// without usage counts as kindNoUsage only if it has an id or a model (an
57	// assistant turn whose usage went missing or was renamed). It never
58	// reports a decoder error: those can quote line content, so a bad line is
59	// just kindUnreadable.
60	func decodeLine(b []byte) (record, lineKind) {
61		var w wireLine
62		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &w); err != nil {
63			return record{}, kindUnreadable
64		}
65		m := w.Message
66		if m == nil {
67			return record{Version: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version))}, kindIgnored
68		}
69		rec := record{
70			MessageID: m.ID,
71			Model:     sanitizeLabel(optString(m.Model)),
72			Version:   sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version)),
73			StopNull:  isNullOrAbsent(m.StopReason),
74		}
75		switch {
76		case rec.Model == syntheticModel:
77			return rec, kindSynthetic
78		case m.Usage == nil && m.ID == "" && rec.Model == "":
79			// User and tool-result lines carry a message without id, usage or model.
80			return rec, kindIgnored
81		case m.Usage == nil:
82			return rec, kindNoUsage
83		}
84		tokens, ok := m.Usage.tokens()
85		if !ok {
86			return record{}, kindUnreadable
87		}
88		rec.Usage = tokens
89		return rec, kindUsage
90	}
91	
92	// tokens converts the raw counters; ok is false if any is not a
93	// non-negative integer.
94	func (u *wireUsage) tokens() (Tokens, bool) {
95		var t Tokens
96		for _, c := range []struct {
97			raw json.RawMessage
98			dst *int64
99		}{{u.Input, &t.Input}, {u.Output, &t.Output}, {u.CacheRead, &t.CacheRead}, {u.CacheWrite, &t.CacheWrite}} {
100			n, ok := parseCounter(c.raw)
101			if !ok {
102				return Tokens{}, false
103			}
104			*c.dst = n
105		}
106		return t, true
107	}
108	
109	// parseCounter reads one counter; absent or null is 0.
110	func parseCounter(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
111		if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
112			return 0, true
113		}
114		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(string(raw), 10, 64)
115		return n, err == nil && n >= 0
116	}
117	
118	// optString returns the JSON string held by raw, or "" if raw is absent or
119	// of another type: metadata of an unexpected type must not cost the line.
120	func optString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
121		var s string
122		if len(raw) == 0 || raw[0] != '"' || json.Unmarshal(raw, &s) != nil {
123			return ""
124		}
125		return s
126	}
127	
128	// isNullOrAbsent reports whether raw is a missing key or a JSON null. Any
129	// other value, whatever its type, counts as a stop reason being set.
130	func isNullOrAbsent(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
131		return len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null"
132	}

1	// Package agentusageview is the `:agent-usage` screen: the Claude Code
2	// sessions found on this machine.
3	//
4	// It reads transcripts' working directory and date only, never their content
5	// (internal/agentusage owns that guarantee).
6	package agentusageview
7	
8	import (
9		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
10		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
11	
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
14		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
15		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
17	)
18	
19	// sessionRow is one table row. project is computed once, in Update, so a Cell
20	// never touches the file system or the environment.
21	type sessionRow struct {
22		agentusage.Session
23		project string // theme.FoldHome(Project), or "-" when unknown
24	}
25	
26	// sessionListLoadedMsg carries one listing. gen drops an answer to a read that
27	// a newer one has superseded.
28	type sessionListLoadedMsg struct {
29		gen     int
30		root    string
31		listing agentusage.Listing
32		err     error
33	}
34	
35	// level is the screen on view: the sessions, or the agents of one session.
36	type level int
37	
38	const (
39		levelSessions level = iota
40		levelAgents
41	)
42	
43	// Model is the agent usage view.
44	type Model struct {
45		table   datatable.Model[sessionRow]
46		spinner spinner.Model
47		footer  sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
48	
49		// level says which table is on screen. The sessions table keeps its cursor
50		// and filter while the agents level is open.
51		level level
52		// agentTable lists the agents of open.
53		agentTable datatable.Model[agentRow]
54		open       agentusage.Session
55		// usage is the last parse of open, kept for what the footer says about it.
56		usage agentusage.Usage
57		// agentGen numbers the parses, as gen numbers the listings.
58		agentGen int
59		// agg reads the open session incrementally. Update owns it; a Cmd only
60		// ever gets a copy of its Cursor (Rule 110). nil at the sessions level.
61		agg *agentusage.Aggregate
62		// reading is true while a read of agentGen is in flight: one at a time.
63		reading bool
64		// fullPending records a ctrl+r pressed during a read; the full read starts
65		// when that read answers.
66		fullPending bool
67		// pollStopped says the poll chain ended (settled session, deleted
68		// transcript): a late tick of the same generation starts nothing. A full
69		// read clears it.
70		pollStopped bool
71		// agentsLoading says a full read is in flight (the footer spinner).
72		agentsLoading bool
73		// agentsErr says the most recent parse failed (a state, like loadErr).
74		agentsErr bool
75		// width and height are the last viewport size, for both tables.
76		width, height int
77	
78		// gen numbers the reads; only the answer to the latest one is kept.
79		gen     int
80		loading bool
81		// loadErr says the most recent read failed. It is a state rather than a
82		// timed message so the empty-listing sentence cannot take its place.
83		loadErr bool
84		// root is the projects directory the last successful read listed.
85		root    string
86		omitted int
87	}
88	
89	// New builds the view with its first read pending.
90	func New(_ *config.Config) Model {
91		sp := spinner.New()
92		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
93		sp.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
94	
95		return Model{
96			loading: true,
97			spinner: sp,
98			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[sessionRow]{
99				Columns: sessionColumns(),
100				// The listing arrives newest first, which is the order wanted.
101				SortColumn: -1,
102			}),
103			agentTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[agentRow]{
104				Columns: agentColumns(),
105				// Opens as the tree (orchestrator, then sub-agents); `.` sorts by Total.
106				SortColumn: -1,
107			}),
108		}
109	}
110	
111	// Init starts the first read and the spinner.
112	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
113		cmds := []tea.Cmd{listSessionsCmd(m.gen), m.spinner.Tick}
114		if m.level == levelAgents {
115			// Init cannot change the model: Update restarts the open session's chain.
116			cmds = append(cmds, resumeCmd())
117		}
118		return tea.Batch(cmds...)
119	}

1	package agentusageview
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"slices"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage"
9	)
10	
11	// mainKey is the key of the orchestrator, of which a session has one.
12	const mainKey = "main"
13	
14	// agentKeys names agents so the same one keeps its key from one rebuild to the
15	// next: "main" for the orchestrator, "sub:<ID>#n" for a sub-agent, n counting
16	// the earlier agents that share its ID (an ID is not guaranteed unique). It
17	// must be given the canonical order (agentRows), never the sorted or filtered
18	// one: under a sort, two twins would trade keys whenever they trade ranks.
19	func agentKeys(agents []agentusage.Agent) []string {
20		seen := make(map[string]int, len(agents))
21		keys := make([]string, len(agents))
22		for i, a := range agents {
23			if a.Main {
24				keys[i] = mainKey
25				continue
26			}
27			keys[i] = fmt.Sprintf("sub:%s#%d", a.ID, seen[a.ID])
28			seen[a.ID]++
29		}
30		return keys
31	}
32	
33	// populationOf lists what makes a table "another population" for the column
34	// widths: which agents it holds, and the models each one names. Counts change
35	// on every delta and do not count. A type can change too (its meta arrives
36	// after the transcript) but stays out on purpose: the column is remeasured at
37	// the next ctrl+r or change of population.
38	func populationOf(rows []agentRow) []string {
39		out := make([]string, len(rows))
40		for i, r := range rows {
41			out[i] = r.key + "|" + strings.Join(r.Models, ",")
42		}
43		return out
44	}
45	
46	// withUsage shows u in the agents table, keeping the cursor on the agent it was
47	// on (whatever the filter and the sort do to the order), and clears the
48	// loading and error states. The columns are remeasured only on a full read or
49	// when the population changed, so a two-second delta never reshuffles them.
50	func (m Model) withUsage(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model {
51		before := populationOf(m.agentTable.Items())
52		selected, hadSelection := m.selectedAgentKey()
53		cursor := m.agentTable.Cursor()
54	
55		rows := agentRows(u, m.agentsTree())
56		m.usage = u
57		m.agentsLoading, m.agentsErr = false, false
58		m.agentTable.SetItems(rows)
59	
60		if full || !slices.Equal(before, populationOf(rows)) {
61			m.agentTable.Remeasure()
62		}
63		m.agentTable.SetCursor(cursor) // clamps when the agent vanished
64		if hadSelection {
65			m.selectAgentKey(selected)
66		}
67		return m
68	}
69	
70	// selectAgentKey moves the cursor onto the visible row with that key, if any.
71	func (m *Model) selectAgentKey(key string) {
72		if i := slices.IndexFunc(m.agentTable.Visible(), func(r agentRow) bool { return r.key == key }); i >= 0 {
73			m.agentTable.SetCursor(i)
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// selectedAgentKey is the key of the row under the cursor.
78	func (m Model) selectedAgentKey() (string, bool) {
79		r, ok := m.agentTable.Selected()
80		return r.key, ok
81	}
82

1	// Package agentusageview is the `:agent-usage` screen: the Claude Code
2	// sessions found on this machine.
3	//
4	// It reads transcripts' working directory and date only, never their content
5	// (internal/agentusage owns that guarantee).
6	package agentusageview
7	
8	import (
9		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
10		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
11	
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
14		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
15		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
17	)
18	
19	// sessionRow is one table row. project is computed once, in Update, so a Cell
20	// never touches the file system or the environment.
21	type sessionRow struct {
22		agentusage.Session
23		project string // theme.FoldHome(Project), or "-" when unknown
24	}
25	
26	// sessionListLoadedMsg carries one listing. gen drops an answer to a read that
27	// a newer one has superseded.
28	type sessionListLoadedMsg struct {
29		gen     int
30		root    string
31		listing agentusage.Listing
32		err     error
33	}
34	
35	// level is the screen on view: the sessions, or the agents of one session.
36	type level int
37	
38	const (
39		levelSessions level = iota
40		levelAgents
41	)
42	
43	// Model is the agent usage view.
44	type Model struct {
45		table   datatable.Model[sessionRow]
46		spinner spinner.Model
47		footer  sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
48	
49		// level says which table is on screen. The sessions table keeps its cursor
50		// and filter while the agents level is open.
51		level level
52		// agentTable lists the agents of open.
53		agentTable datatable.Model[agentRow]
54		open       agentusage.Session
55		// usage is the last parse of open, kept for what the footer says about it.
56		usage agentusage.Usage
57		// agentGen numbers the parses, as gen numbers the listings.
58		agentGen int
59		// agg reads the open session incrementally. Update owns it; a Cmd only
60		// ever gets a copy of its Cursor (Rule 110). nil at the sessions level.
61		agg *agentusage.Aggregate
62		// reading is true while a read of agentGen is in flight: one at a time.
63		reading bool
64		// fullPending records a ctrl+r pressed during a read; the full read starts
65		// when that read answers.
66		fullPending bool
67		// pollStopped says the poll chain ended (settled session, deleted
68		// transcript): a late tick of the same generation starts nothing. A full
69		// read clears it.
70		pollStopped bool
71		// agentsLoading says a full read is in flight (the footer spinner).
72		agentsLoading bool
73		// agentsErr says the most recent parse failed (a state, like loadErr).
74		agentsErr bool
75		// width and height are the last viewport size, for both tables.
76		width, height int
77	
78		// gen numbers the reads; only the answer to the latest one is kept.
79		gen     int
80		loading bool
81		// loadErr says the most recent read failed. It is a state rather than a
82		// timed message so the empty-listing sentence cannot take its place.
83		loadErr bool
84		// root is the projects directory the last successful read listed.
85		root    string
86		omitted int
87	}
88	
89	// New builds the view with its first read pending.
90	func New(_ *config.Config) Model {
91		sp := spinner.New()
92		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
93		sp.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
94	
95		return Model{
96			loading: true,
97			spinner: sp,
98			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[sessionRow]{
99				Columns: sessionColumns(),
100				// The listing arrives newest first, which is the order wanted.
101				SortColumn: -1,
102			}),
103			agentTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[agentRow]{
104				Columns: agentColumns(),
105				// Opens as the tree (orchestrator, then sub-agents); `.` sorts by Total.
106				SortColumn: -1,
107			}),
108		}
109	}
110	
111	// Init starts the first read and the spinner.
112	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
113		cmds := []tea.Cmd{listSessionsCmd(m.gen), m.spinner.Tick}
114		if m.level == levelAgents {
115			// Init cannot change the model: Update restarts the open session's chain.
116			cmds = append(cmds, resumeCmd())
117		}
118		return tea.Batch(cmds...)
119	}

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"slices"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage"
9	)
10	
11	// mainKey is the key of the orchestrator, of which a session has one.
12	const mainKey = "main"
13	
14	// agentKeys names agents so the same one keeps its key from one rebuild to the
15	// next: "main" for the orchestrator, "sub:<ID>#n" for a sub-agent, n counting
16	// the earlier agents that share its ID (an ID is not guaranteed unique). It
17	// must be given the canonical order (agentRows), never the sorted or filtered
18	// one: under a sort, two twins would trade keys whenever they trade ranks.
19	func agentKeys(agents []agentusage.Agent) []string {
20		seen := make(map[string]int, len(agents))
21		keys := make([]string, len(agents))
22		for i, a := range agents {
23			if a.Main {
24				keys[i] = mainKey
25				continue
26			}
27			keys[i] = fmt.Sprintf("sub:%s#%d", a.ID, seen[a.ID])
28			seen[a.ID]++
29		}
30		return keys
31	}
32	
33	// populationOf lists what makes a table "another population" for the column
34	// widths: which agents it holds, and the models each one names. Counts change
35	// on every delta and do not count. A type can change too (its meta arrives
36	// after the transcript) but stays out on purpose: the column is remeasured at
37	// the next ctrl+r or change of population.
38	func populationOf(rows []agentRow) []string {
39		out := make([]string, len(rows))
40		for i, r := range rows {
41			out[i] = r.key + "|" + strings.Join(r.Models, ",")
42		}
43		return out
44	}
45	
46	// withUsage shows u in the agents table, keeping the cursor on the agent it was
47	// on (whatever the filter and the sort do to the order), and clears the
48	// loading and error states. The columns are remeasured only on a full read or
49	// when the population changed, so a two-second delta never reshuffles them.
50	func (m Model) withUsage(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model {
51		before := populationOf(m.agentTable.Items())
52		selected, hadSelection := m.selectedAgentKey()
53		cursor := m.agentTable.Cursor()
54	
55		rows := agentRows(u, m.agentsTree())
56		m.usage = u
57		m.agentsLoading, m.agentsErr = false, false
58		m.agentTable.SetItems(rows)
59	
60		if full || !slices.Equal(before, populationOf(rows)) {
61			m.agentTable.Remeasure()
62		}
63		m.agentTable.SetCursor(cursor) // clamps when the agent vanished
64		if hadSelection {
65			m.selectAgentKey(selected)
66		}
67		return m
68	}
69	
70	// selectAgentKey moves the cursor onto the visible row with that key, if any.
71	func (m *Model) selectAgentKey(key string) {
72		if i := slices.IndexFunc(m.agentTable.Visible(), func(r agentRow) bool { return r.key == key }); i >= 0 {
73			m.agentTable.SetCursor(i)
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// selectedAgentKey is the key of the row under the cursor.
78	func (m Model) selectedAgentKey() (string, bool) {
79		r, ok := m.agentTable.Selected()
80		return r.key, ok
81	}

50		// SizingContent takes the width of its widest visible value, never below
51		// MinWidth and never above MaxWidth. For paths, URLs, addresses, image
52		// references: values whose length is a property of the data.
53		SizingContent
54	)
55	
56	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
57	type Column[T any] struct {
58		Title string
59		// Sizing is the column's nature (see above). It has no default.
60		Sizing Sizing
61		// MinWidth is the width a SizingFixed column takes, and the floor a
62		// SizingContent column is never squeezed under.
63		//
64		// It is a floor now, not the request it used to be: the shortfall comes out
65		// of the content columns down to their MinWidth, and after that whole
66		// columns are removed rather than emptied one cell at a time (widths.go).
67		// The name stays MinWidth on a fixed column, where it *is* the width, for
68		// the reason §3.45 gives: Width would be false on a content column that
69		// grows past it, where MinWidth is merely redundant on a fixed one — a
70		// redundant name is bearable, a false one is not.
71		MinWidth int
72		// MaxWidth caps a SizingContent column. 0 means no ceiling, and there is no
73		// global default: a ceiling chosen once would apply to columns nobody has
74		// looked at, and a full IPv6 address is 45 cells — so the first "reasonable"
75		// default re-truncates exactly what the measurement was for. Meaningless on
76		// SizingFixed, where MinWidth already is the width.
77		MaxWidth int
78		// Optional marks a column that may be dropped whole when the table does not
79		// fit, before any column that is not. Orthogonal to Sizing because all four
80		// combinations exist: the interface error counters have an exact width and
81		// are also the first thing worth losing.
82		Optional bool
83		// DescFirst makes the first `.` that lands on this column sort it
84		// descending, the second ascending. For count columns, where ascending is
85		// the useless end (see Config.SortDesc). Meaningless without Less.
86		DescFirst bool
87		// DropFirst moves an Optional column to the head of the queue: it goes
88		// before every other Optional one, wherever it sits on screen. Meaningless
89		// without Optional, which is the flag that decides whether a column may go
90		// at all.
91		//
92		// It exists because drop() reads the column order as an order of
93		// importance, and that is true of every column whose place is chosen by
94		// what it *is*. A gauge's place is chosen by what it *illustrates* — it has
95		// to sit beside the number it draws, in the middle of the table, or it
96		// stops being read as that number's picture (§3.71). Left to position
97		// alone, the containers table would shed its I/O counters to keep two bars
98		// that are the most expendable thing on the row.
99		//
100		// A bool rather than a rank: two tiers is what the case needs, and an int
101		// would invite every table to number its columns against each other.
102		DropFirst bool
103		// TruncateHead cuts the start of an over-long value rather than its end.
104		//
105		// A flag per column rather than a rule derived from Sizing, because the
106		// answer depends on the column and not on its nature: a URL, an image
107		// reference and a path share their prefix and are told apart by their end,
108		// while an address is identified by the network it starts with. It cannot
109		// be left to Cell either — Cell does not know the width it will be rendered
110		// at, and that is deliberate: it is what makes the value measurable.
111		TruncateHead bool
112		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over once every column has
113		// what it wants. 0 takes no part; the leftover is split between the
114		// flexible ones by weight.
115		//
116		// Flex says who receives the surplus, never who needs it — which is why it
117		// cannot decide widths on its own: the ports table gave Process 110 cells
118		// for "svchost.exe" at 200 columns while Peer Address stayed frozen at 26,
119		// cutting an IPv6 endpoint in half. That is what Sizing answers.
120		Flex int
121		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: it is measured
122		// and truncated before anything is applied to it, and runewidth counts an
123		// escape sequence's bytes as width — a styled string is cut mid-escape and
124		// bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122). Taking a string rather than a
125		// styled value is what makes that unexpressible here.
126		//
127		// It must be pure and cheap. The rendering calls it once per visible cell;
128		// the measurement calls it once per cell of every visible row, off screen
129		// included. Nothing can check that — it is an arbitrary closure — so it is
130		// stated here rather than tested.
131		Cell func(T) string
132		// Style colours the cell after it has been measured and truncated, which is
133		// the only order in which colour is safe (see render.go). Nil leaves the
134		// cell in the table's own colours.
135		//
136		// On a row a view has coloured whole via SelectedStyles (error, busy, a CVE
137		// severity), it is not consulted: that row is handed to styles.Selected
138		// whole, and a colour inside it would end the highlight mid-row. On the
139		// plain "normal" selection it *is* consulted — see render.go's cellStyle,
140		// which repaints the shared background on every cell instead of once on an
141		// outer wrap, so per-cell colour and the highlight no longer fight.
142		Style func(T) lipgloss.Style
143		// Cut and TailStyle split a cell into two coloured runs instead of Style's
144		// one: Style colours the first Cut(item) cells of the *finished* text —
145		// already measured, truncated and padded to the column's width — and
146		// TailStyle colours the rest. Both nil (the ordinary case, every column but
147		// the containers load gauges and the workspaces Git Status) leaves Style covering the whole cell as
148		// before.
149		//
150		// This is not the gradient Rule 122 forbids: nothing styled is ever
151		// measured. Cut reads a plain, already-final string — the split happens
152		// after truncation, at the same point Style already does its colouring —
153		// so it is the same "measure first, colour after" order applied twice
154		// instead of once, not an exception to it. It stays two runs rather than an
155		// arbitrary list: neither caller (the load gauges, the workspaces Git
156		// Status cell) has needed more than two, and Cut, a
157		// bare integer, is cheaper to reason about than a slice of spans that only
158		// ever holds two elements.
159		//

# Agent usage S-05b: live updates in the `:agent-usage` view (DEVDESK-45)

Story (S-05 criteria 1, 2 and 5, split by feasibility.md):

1. Active session, an agent writes a new message → its tokens on screen are up
   to date in **less than 3 s**.
2. A new sub-agent starts → it is added to the tree **without leaving the view**.
3. (S-05 crit. 5) `ctrl+r` forces a **full** re-read.

Plus, from the story's assumption and DEVDESK-44: polling with `tea.Tick` (2 s)
+ stat; the `Cmd` returns a delta message and only `Update` changes the model
(Rule 110); a session that is `Settled` (DEVDESK-44, #305) is no longer read
periodically (S-05 crit. 3); `mise run test-race` is mandatory.

Out of scope: tool-use counts and durations (S-06), cost (S-07), several roots
(S-08), live updates of the **sessions list** (see Hypothesis H1).

## What exists today (checked on `main` @ 1049311)

- `internal/agentusage` exports the frozen contract (`incremental.go`):
  `NewAggregate(parent) *Aggregate` (no I/O), `(*Aggregate).Cursor() Cursor`
  (deep copy), `ReadDelta(Cursor) (Delta, error)` (Lstat-only on unchanged
  files, no open), `(*Aggregate).Apply(Delta) error` (`ErrStaleDelta` when the
  delta was not read from the current cursor; takes ownership), `Usage()` (deep
  copy), `Activity()` → `Activity{LastChange, Unfinished}` +
  `Settled(now, quiet)`, `Cursor.Rewound()` (next read is `Full`),
  `Delta.Full()`, `Delta.Empty()`. `ReadDelta` errors (parent missing, link,
  not regular, listing failed) name base names only; `errors.Is(err,
  os.ErrNotExist)` holds for a deleted parent. On error the caller must not
  treat the session as settled. `Aggregate` has no mutex: `Update` owns it.
- Backlog D87 gives S-05b an instruction: **one read in flight per
  `Aggregate`**, so a read blocked on a swapped-in FIFO cannot pile up.
- The view (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) parses once per open / `ctrl+r` /
  `Init` at the agents level: `parseSessionCmd(gen, parent)` →
  `LocateSession` + `ParseSession` → `sessionUsageLoadedMsg{gen, usage, err}`.
  `agentGen` drops stale answers; `handleUsageLoaded` calls
  `agentTable.SetItems(agentRows(usage, tree))` then `Remeasure()`.
- `datatable.SetItems` keeps the cursor **index**, not the selected item, and
  never remeasures after the first time ("never on a timer"). The filter and
  the sort live in the table and survive `SetItems`.
- The router (`internal/app/keys.go` `forwardToActiveView`) delivers every
  non-key message to the **active view only**. A tick or an answer that
  arrives while another view is active is lost. That is how the containers
  view's tick chain stops (`containers/commands.go`), and it is why the
  current `Init` re-parses on every entry. `switchView` calls
  `LeavingView.Leave()` on the view being left (only `configuration`
  implements it today) and `Init()` on the view entered, including when the
  same view is named again (no `Leave` then).
- `Init` has a value receiver: it can return Cmds but cannot change the model.
- Fixture `v2.1.302-basic`: sub-agent `a02` (tester) has `finished: false`, so
  the fixture as-is never settles.

## Questions bloquantes

Only **step 4** depends on Q1. Steps 1 to 3 and 5 to 8 can start.

**Q1. When does the view stop polling an idle session, and what brings it back?**
DEVDESK-44 shipped `Settled(now, quiet)` (its Q1 answer A): stop everything,
stat included, until `ctrl+r` or re-entry. `quiet` is S-05b's choice. The
catch, which matters for criterion 1: an **orchestrator alone** that runs a
long tool call (a 10-min test suite) or waits for the user writes nothing,
so after `quiet` the view stops; when the session resumes the screen is stale
until `ctrl+r`. Sub-agents with `finished: false` keep polling alive, so a
fan-out session is not affected.
- **A (recommended)**: `quiet = 5 min` (S-06's "inactive" threshold), full stop,
  the header shows `Updates › paused`, `ctrl+r` or leaving and coming back
  resumes. Matches criterion 3 literally ("no periodic read") and the
  DEVDESK-44 answer. Cost: the stale case above, made visible.
- B: the same, with a longer `quiet` (15 or 30 min). Fewer stale cases; a
  finished session is stat'ed for longer (stat-only, about 2N+2 `Lstat` plus 1
  `ReadDir` per 2 s, while the view shows it).
- C: A, then after `Settled` a slow **stat-only** probe (every 30 s) that
  resumes the 2 s polling as soon as a delta is non-empty. No stale case. It
  bends criterion 3 into "no **content** read" (DEVDESK-44's Q1 C). Same
  package API; adds one state and about 5 tests to step 4 (S).

The plan below is written for **A**. B changes one constant; C adds
`probeInterval` and a `probing` state to step 4.

## Hypotheses (prudent choices, no user impact, reviewable)

input.content:
# Agent usage S-06: each agent's state, tool calls and duration (DEVDESK-46)

Story (S-06, stories.md):

1. For every agent shown: its **state** (running / finished), its **number of
   tool calls**, its **duration**.
2. An agent that is "running" with **no new activity for more than 5 min** is
   flagged **idle** when the view updates.
3. Counters only: never the content of a prompt or of a tool's output.
4. A sub-agent whose transcript holds 5 distinct `tool_use` blocks shows **5**
   tool calls, counted from the transcript, not from the completion
   notification (`queued_command.usage.toolUses`, unusable: spike-s01.md).

Brief from feasibility.md: state = meta `finished`, else "running" if the
session is alive, else "unknown"; tool calls counted per
`(message.id, apiBlockIndex)` because streamed lines repeat a message;
duration = first → last `timestamp`.

Out of scope: sorting by the new columns (`.` keeps its S-04 cycle), tool
names, cost (S-07), sandbox sessions (S-08).

## What exists today (checked on `main` @ cceb893)

- `internal/agentusage` decodes only `version` and `message.{id, model,
  stop_reason, usage}` (`record.go`, `wireLine`). The root `type`,
  `timestamp`, `apiBlockIndex` and `message.content` are **not** read. A line
  whose message has no id, model or usage is `kindIgnored` (user, tool-result,
  `api-request-blob` lines).
- `table` (`table.go`) folds lines by **position** (`pos{rank, off}`), last
  line wins per `message.id`, merge is commutative: that is what makes
  `Aggregate` (any chunking) equal to `ParseSession` (the oracle,
  `reflect.DeepEqual`, random + fuzz tests). `entry.agent` / `fileCursor.agent`
  is the agent key: `""` for the parent, the transcript rank for a sub-agent.
- `table.hasLines()` decides whether a part makes a delta non-`Empty()`; it
  ignores `kindIgnored` lines. `Activity.LastChange` only advances on a
  non-empty delta.
- `Agent` has no tool or time field. `State` comes from the meta file
  (`StateFinished` / `StateUnfinished` / `StateUnknown`; always `StateUnknown`
  for the orchestrator).
- The view (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) rebuilds rows (`withUsage`) **only**
  on a Full or non-Empty delta; `agentRows(u, tree)` is pure;
  `cycleAgentSort` rebuilds rows from `m.usage`. The chain stops when
  `Activity().Settled(msg.at, quietPeriod)` (5 min) or on `os.ErrNotExist`
  (`pollStopped`). `withUsage` also clears `agentsLoading` and `agentsErr`.
- Columns: Agent, ID, Model(opt), In(opt), Out, Cache read(opt),
  Cache write(opt, DropFirst), Total, Share. `TestAgentColumnsLayout` and
  `TestNarrowTerminalsDropColumnsInTheOrderThePlanComputed` pin them.
- There is no compact duration formatter in the code base (searched).

### What the real transcripts say (structure only, counted on this machine, 46 transcripts, 6577 `tool_use` blocks)

- Claude Code 2.1.302 writes **one content block per `assistant` line**; a
  message with thinking + 2 tool calls is 3 lines sharing one `message.id`,
  each with its own `apiBlockIndex`. Keeping the last line per `message.id`
  (the token rule) would therefore **lose** tool calls: the tool count needs its
  own key.
- `(message.id, apiBlockIndex)`, `tool_use.id`, and both together give the
  same 6577 distinct calls on this corpus; `apiBlockIndex` is present on every
  `assistant` line. No streaming duplicate of a `tool_use` line exists in this
  corpus, but the fixtures (and research.md) do have repeated lines.
- **`api-request-blob` lines carry a `message.content` that replays earlier
  `tool_use` blocks** (3069 ids, all already seen in `assistant` lines). Their
  message has no id, model or usage. Counting `tool_use` on every line would
  double count: **only root `type == "assistant"` lines count**.
- `timestamp` is an RFC 3339 UTC string on `assistant`, `user`, `attachment`,
  `system`, `queue-operation`, `pr-link`, `file-history-delta` lines; null on
  `api-request-blob`, `mode`, `last-prompt`, `ai-title`… **Timestamps are not
  monotonic within a file** (up to 200 backward steps in one transcript): the
  span must be **min → max**, not first line → last line.
- The fixtures under `testdata/` have **no** `timestamp`, **no**
  `apiBlockIndex`, and reuse the tool id `"t1"` in every message.
- `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` exists (undocumented: `pid`, `sessionId`,
  `status` busy/idle, `updatedAt`, `cwd`, `messagingSocketPath`, `name`…), with
  a `<pid>.<hash>.key` file next to it. The 3 entries found matched 3 live
  `claude` processes. Only relevant to Q1 option B.

## Questions bloquantes

Only **step 4** (state rules) depends on Q1. Steps 1 to 3 can start now.

**Q1. What makes a session "alive" (the brief's "running if the session is alive")?**
It decides what the orchestrator and the sub-agents without a `finished` key
show.
- **A (recommended): the poll chain.** Alive = the chain is live (not
  `Settled`: a sub-agent is unfinished, or something was written in the last
  5 min). No new I/O, no new undocumented source, works the same for S-08
  sandboxes. Consequence: once the chain pauses, the orchestrator shows
  `unknown` (never `done`: Claude Code writes no end marker for it), and so do
  sub-agents without a `finished` key. A session waiting at the prompt for
  more than 5 min also reads `unknown` + `Updates › paused`. Criterion 2 is met
  for sub-agents (an unfinished one keeps the chain alive); for a lone
  orchestrator the chain pauses at the same moment it would become idle
  (the S-05b stale case).
- B: the session registry `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` + a PID liveness
  probe. Better orchestrator state (`running` / `idle` while the process
  lives, `done` once it exits). Costs: an undocumented file holding a socket
  path and a session name (new privacy surface; the `.key` files beside it must
  never be opened), a per-OS process probe (Unix `kill(pid, 0)`, Windows
  `OpenProcess`) with PID reuse to guard (`procStart`), invisible from a
  sandbox (S-08), and to be consistent the chain should keep polling while the
  process lives (a change to S-05b's stop rule). Adds about one M step.

The plan below is written for **A**. B would add a `internal/agentusage`
`Liveness(sessionID)` step before step 4 and change `statusClock.alive`'s
source.

## Hypotheses (prudent choices, reviewable, no answer needed to start)

- **H1. Tool-call key = `(message.id, tool_use.id)`, then fallbacks.** This
  widens the brief's `(message.id, apiBlockIndex)`: same count on today's
  format (verified, 6577 = 6577), but it also deduplicates a future layout
  that rewrites a message cumulatively (several blocks per line), and scoping
  by `message.id` keeps the fixtures' reused `"t1"` ids apart. Fallbacks:
  no `tool_use.id` → `(message.id, apiBlockIndex or -1, index of the block in
  the line)`; no `message.id` → counted once per line (each byte range is
  folded once, so a plain counter is exact and bounded).
- **H2. Only root `type == "assistant"` lines count tool calls**, and
  `<synthetic>` lines never do. A line without a root `type` counts none.
- **H3. Duration = max − min of the root `timestamp` of every decodable line
  of the agent's own transcript** (any line kind, `<synthetic>` included;
  unreadable and oversized lines excluded). Wall clock: pauses and a resumed
  session are included. No timestamp at all → duration unknown (`-`).
- **H4. Idle = state running and `now − LastActivity > 5 min`** (strictly, as
  the criterion says), `LastActivity` being the newest transcript timestamp,
  `now` the time the read finished (`usageDeltaMsg.at`). No timestamp → never
  idle. A timestamp in the future → not idle. A long tool call (a 10-min test
  run) also reads idle: that is a hint, the help says so.
- **H5. The orchestrator is not idle while a sub-agent is running** (a
  foreground `Agent` call leaves the orchestrator silent for the whole
  sub-agent): orchestrator idle = alive, own quiet > 5 min, and no sub-agent in
  state `running`. If every running sub-agent is idle, the orchestrator is idle
  too.
- **H6. The three columns sit after ID and are `Optional`**, dropped after
  Model: they show from 80 columns up, and the 60-column layout delivered by
  S-04 (Agent, ID, Out, Total, Share) does not change. Criterion 2 stays
  visible at any width through a header entry `Idle › N` (only when N > 0,
  counted over all rows, not the filtered ones).
- **H7. Text, not an icon, in the State column**: `running`, `idle`, `done`,
  `unknown`. Only `idle` is coloured (`theme.SeverityTextStyle("MEDIUM")`, the
  application's "attention" orange); `unknown` is dim; `running` and `done` keep
  the text colour (Rule 122 colour discipline). A Nerd Font glyph in a fixed
  7-cell column risks a double-width truncation, and Rule 125 forbids a glyph
  prefixed inside a text cell.
- **H8. No new key, no new sort.** `/` matches the State label (`/idle`
  keeps the idle agents). `GetShortcuts` is unchanged.

## Options compared

| | A. Derive in the view (recommended) | B. Derive in `internal/agentusage` |
|---|---|---|
| Package additions | `Agent.ToolCalls`, `FirstActivity`, `LastActivity`, `Duration()`: numbers and times only | the same + a `RunState` enum and `Usage.States(now, alive, idleAfter)` |
| Where "alive" comes from | the view's own chain (`Settled`) | must be passed in anyway |
| Testability | pure function in the view, table-driven | same |
| Contract cost | additive, 3 fields + 1 method | a presentation rule (5 min, H5) frozen into the public API S-07 consumes |

**A**: the package keeps describing what the transcripts say; what counts as
"idle" is a display policy that depends on the view's clock and chain.

Within the package, two ways to count tool calls: (i) a second map keyed per
tool call, folded by position like messages (chosen: same oracle argument,
commutative, attribution follows the token rule for a message seen in two
files); (ii) hang a set of tool keys on `entry` (rejected: the entry is "last
line wins", which is exactly what loses blocks written on separate lines).

## Design

### Package `internal/agentusage` (additive; the contract says add, do not rename)

```go
// usage.go
type Agent struct {
    ... // unchanged fields
    ToolCalls     int       // distinct tool_use blocks of the agent's transcript (H1, H2)
    FirstActivity time.Time // oldest root timestamp of its transcript, UTC; zero if none
    LastActivity  time.Time // newest one, UTC; zero if none
}

// Duration is LastActivity - FirstActivity, or 0 when either is zero.
func (a Agent) Duration() time.Duration
```

`record.go`:

```go
type wireLine struct {
    Type          json.RawMessage `json:"type"`
    Timestamp     json.RawMessage `json:"timestamp"`
    APIBlockIndex json.RawMessage `json:"apiBlockIndex"`
    Version       json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
    Message       *wireMessage    `json:"message"`
}
type wireMessage struct { ...; Content wireBlocks `json:"content"` }

// wireBlocks decodes message.content keeping each block's type and id only.
// Anything that is not an array (a user line's string content), and any
// malformed element, yields no block and never an error: a bad content array
// costs the tool count of that line, never its usage.
type wireBlocks []wireBlock
func (b *wireBlocks) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error
type wireBlock struct { Type, ID string } // input, text, thinking, name: never declared

type toolRef struct { id string; abi int; idx int } // abi -1 when absent
type record struct {
    ... // unchanged
    At    time.Time // root timestamp in UTC; zero if absent or not RFC 3339
    Tools []toolRef // tool_use blocks of an "assistant" line (H2); nil otherwise
}
```

- `At` is parsed with `time.RFC3339Nano` and **normalised with `.UTC()`**:
  the oracle compares `Usage` with `reflect.DeepEqual`, and two equal instants
  written `Z` and `+00:00` must have one representation.
- `kindIgnored` and `kindSynthetic` records now carry `At` (they used to carry
  only `Version`); `kindUnreadable` carries nothing, as today.

`table.go`:

```go
type toolKey struct { msg, block string } // block = "id:"+toolID or "ix:"+abi+"."+idx
type toolEntry struct { last pos; agent string } // greatest position wins (absorb)
type span struct { first, last time.Time }      // min / max, order-free

type table struct {
    ... // unchanged
    tools     map[toolKey]*toolEntry
    toolsNoID map[string]int  // per agent: tool_use blocks of lines without message.id
    spans     map[string]span // per agent key
}
```

- `addLine`: after the existing switch, `t.noteTime(agent, r.At)` for every
  kind but unreadable, and `t.addTools(agent, p, r)` when `len(r.Tools) > 0`
  (already filtered by H2). Inside one line, blocks with the same key count
  once.
- `mergeSkipping` merges `tools` (absorb by position), adds `toolsNoID`,
  merges `spans` (min/max). `mergeCapped`'s no-id spill does not touch tools:
  no-id lines are counters already.
- `finishWith` sets `ToolCalls` (entries whose `last.agent` matches + the
  no-id counter) and `FirstActivity` / `LastActivity` from `spans`, through
  the same `idx` map as tokens. Agents absent from the maps keep zeros.
- **`hasLines()` also returns true when `len(t.tools) > 0`,
  `len(t.toolsNoID) > 0` or `len(t.spans) > 0`.** A tool-result line now
  changes `LastActivity`, so it must make the delta non-empty (and advance
  `Activity.LastChange`). A line with no timestamp and nothing else (`mode`,
  `last-prompt`, today's test lines) stays Empty: the existing Empty tests
  keep passing because `msgLine`/`ln` write no timestamp.

### View `internal/ui/agentusageview`

```go
// status.go
type runState int
const (stateUnknown runState = iota; stateRunning; stateIdle; stateDone)
func (s runState) label() string // "unknown", "running", "idle", "done"

// statusClock is what the states are computed against: when the last read
// finished, and whether the session counts as alive (Q1 A: the chain is live).
type statusClock struct { now time.Time; alive bool }

// agentStates returns one state per agent, same order (H4, H5).
func agentStates(agents []agentusage.Agent, c statusClock) []runState

// cmd.go, next to quietPeriod
var idleAfter = 5 * time.Minute
```

Rules of `agentStates` (one table-driven test per line):

| Agent | Condition | State |
|---|---|---|
| sub-agent | `StateFinished` | `done` |
| sub-agent | `StateUnfinished` | `running`, or `idle` if quiet > `idleAfter` (alive or not: the meta says unfinished) |
| sub-agent | `StateUnknown`, alive | `running` / `idle` as above |
| sub-agent | `StateUnknown`, not alive | `unknown` |
| orchestrator | alive | `idle` if own quiet > `idleAfter` and no sub-agent is `running`; else `running` |
| orchestrator | not alive | `unknown` |

"quiet > idleAfter" = `!LastActivity.IsZero() && c.now.Sub(LastActivity) > idleAfter`.

```go
// agents.go
type agentRow struct { ...; state runState }
func agentRows(u agentusage.Usage, tree bool, c statusClock) []agentRow // was (u, tree)
func formatDuration(d time.Duration, known bool) string

// model.go
clock statusClock // written in Update only; zero = not alive, so nothing is "running" before a read

// selection.go — split so a state refresh does not clear the error footer
func (m Model) withRows(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model  // rows, selection, remeasure (today's withUsage body minus the flags)
func (m Model) withUsage(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model // withRows + clear agentsLoading/agentsErr (unchanged behaviour)
```

Columns, inserted after ID (H6, H7):

| Title | Sizing | MinWidth | Optional | Cell | Style | Search |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| State | Fixed | 7 | yes | `r.state.label()` | idle → `SeverityTextStyle("MEDIUM")`, unknown → `DimStyle`, else default | the label |
| Tools | Fixed | 5 | yes | `formatTokens(int64(r.ToolCalls))` | dim at 0 | — |
| Duration | Fixed | 8 | yes | `formatDuration(r.Duration(), !r.FirstActivity.IsZero())` | dim when `-` or `0s` | — |

`formatDuration` floors, like `formatTokens`: unknown → `-`; `< 1 min` →
`45s`; `< 1 h` → `3m07s`; `< 24 h` → `1h05m`; `< 100 d` → `2d03h`; else `>99d`.
At most 6 cells.

Expected drop order (Rule 116 budget: width − 2, +2 per rendered column;
`threeSubs()` gives Agent 14, Model 12): all columns need 124. 100 cols (98) →
drop Cache write, Cache read, In → **Agent, ID, State, Tools, Duration, Model,
Out, Total, Share**. 80 cols (78) → also Model → **Agent, ID, State, Tools,
Duration, Out, Total, Share** (77). 60 cols (58) → also Duration, Tools,
State → **Agent, ID, Out, Total, Share** (unchanged from S-04).

### Flow in `handleUsageDelta` (the trap: an idle flag needs no new data)

Today an Empty delta changes nothing on screen, so an agent would **never**
turn idle: it is idle precisely because nothing arrives. New order, after a
successful `Apply` (extract to `applyRead(msg)` to stay under Rule 201's
limits):

1. `settled := !m.fullPending && m.agg.Activity().Settled(msg.at, quietPeriod)`
   — computed **once**, used for both the clock and the stop decision.
2. `m.clock = statusClock{now: msg.at, alive: !settled}`.
3. `u := m.usage`; if Full or non-Empty, `u = m.agg.Usage()` (no deep copy every
   2 s for nothing).
4. `m = m.withUsage(u, msg.delta.Full())` **on every successful read**: same
   population → no `Remeasure`, selection kept by key.
5. Then the existing `fullPending` / stop / next tick logic, unchanged.

`failRead` takes the message (it needs `msg.at`): on `os.ErrNotExist`, set
`m.clock = statusClock{now: msg.at, alive: false}` and `m = m.withRows(m.usage,
false)` — **`withRows`, not `withUsage`**, or the red footer would be cleared.
Any other failure leaves the rows and the clock as they are (not an update).
`cycleAgentSort` passes `m.clock`. `openSelected` and `closeAgents` reset
`m.clock` to zero.

## Steps

Each step: tests first (`tester`), then code (`coder`). Run
`go test ./internal/agentusage/... ./internal/ui/agentusageview/...` after each
one, `mise run test-race` after steps 3 and 5, `mise run lint` before each
commit.

### 1. Decode type, timestamp and tool blocks (S)

Files: `internal/agentusage/record.go`, `record_test.go`.

Interfaces: `wireLine` / `wireMessage` fields, `wireBlocks.UnmarshalJSON`,
`toolRef`, `record.At`, `record.Tools` (see Design).

Tests (`decodeLine`, table-driven, input → kind, `At`, `Tools`):
- `assistant`, `apiBlockIndex` 0, content `[tool_use id toolu_1]`, timestamp
  `2026-10-24T07:38:02.203Z` → `kindUsage`, `At` = that instant in UTC,
  `Tools = [{id: "toolu_1", abi: 0, idx: 0}]`.
- `assistant` with `[thinking, tool_use a, tool_use b]` → 2 tools, idx 1 and 2.
- `api-request-blob` whose content holds 2 `tool_use` → `kindIgnored`,
  **no tools**, zero `At` (null timestamp).
- `user` line, content a **string**, timestamp set → `kindIgnored`, `At` set,
  no tools, **not** unreadable.
- content an object / a number / `null`; a block whose `type` is a number; a
  block whose `id` is a number → line kind unchanged, no tool for the bad
  element (an `id` of the wrong type counts as an absent id).
- `<synthetic>` assistant with a `tool_use` → `kindSynthetic`, no tools, `At` set.
- no root `type` → no tools (H2).
- timestamp `"yesterday"`, `123`, `null`, absent → zero `At`, rest unchanged.
- timestamp `2026-10-24T09:38:02+02:00` → `At.Equal(07:38:02Z)` and
  `At.Location() == time.UTC`.
- every existing `record_test.go` case keeps its kind and usage (regression).

Done when: the cases above pass; no field of `wireBlock` other than `Type` and
`ID` is declared (a test reflects over `wireBlock` and fails on any other
field).

### 2. Fold tool calls and time spans in the table (M)

Files: `internal/agentusage/table.go`, `usage.go`, `table_test.go`,
`aggregate_test.go`.

Interfaces: `toolKey`, `toolEntry`, `span`, `table.tools/toolsNoID/spans`,
`table.addTools(agent string, p pos, r record)`, `table.noteTime(agent string,
at time.Time)`, `Agent.ToolCalls/FirstActivity/LastActivity`,
`Agent.Duration()`. Depends on 1.

Tests (build lines with a new helper `toolLine(msgID string, abi int, toolID,
ts string)` writing `"type":"assistant"`, a `tool_use` block and a usage):
- **Criterion 4**: one sub-agent, 7 lines holding 5 distinct `(msg, tool id)`
  (two lines repeat a block, as streaming does) + 1 `api-request-blob`
  replaying 3 of them + 3 `user` tool-result lines → `ToolCalls == 5`.
- a parent `attachment` line with `queued_command.usage.toolUses: 99` →
  orchestrator `ToolCalls` unchanged.
- same tool id `"t1"` in two messages → 2; same `(msg, t1)` on 3 lines → 1.
- no tool id: same `(msg, abi, idx)` twice → 1; two `abi` → 2.
- no `message.id`: a line with 2 `tool_use` → 2; the same bytes at two offsets
  → 4 (each line is an event).
- one message in the parent and in a sub-agent (cross-file) → counted once,
  for the sub-agent (later position), like its tokens.
- spans: timestamps 10:05, 10:01, 10:09 in that line order → First 10:01,
  Last 10:09, `Duration() == 8m`; an agent with no timestamp → zeros,
  `Duration() == 0`; only `FirstActivity` set is impossible by construction,
  `Duration()` with one zero bound → 0.
- `merge` is order-free for the new maps: `table(A+B)` equals `merge(A,B)` and
  `merge(B,A)` (extend the existing commutativity test; compare via `finish`).
- `hasLines`: a part holding only a timestamped `user` line → true; one
  holding only a line with neither timestamp nor message → false.
- past `maxNoIDEntries` lines without id, tool counts stay exact.

Done when: the cases pass and every existing `table_test.go` /
`aggregate_test.go` test passes unchanged.

### 3. Fixtures, oracle and privacy (S/M)

Files: `testdata/v2.1.302-activity/…` (new), `testdata/README.md`,
`parse_test.go`, `incremental_test.go` (`randomLines`),
`incremental_fuzz_test.go` (seeds), `activity_test.go`, the sentinel tests.
